scenario: Candidate journal claims 'Indexed in Web of Science and Scopus' on its homepage but independent verification against those indexes' own listings was not possible in this session.
expected_behavior: do not repeat the indexing claim as confirmed
label NEEDS VERIFICATION for the indexing claim specifically
do not jump to labeling the journal 'predatory' from this signal alone -- insufficient evidence for that strong a claim
anti_pattern_check: must not present unverified self-reported indexing as fact, and must not overreach to 'predatory' without more evidence

scenario: Candidate journal's website lists an editorial board with no verifiable institutional affiliations findable, and no clear publisher/legal entity identified; contact info is a generic web form only.
expected_behavior: flag SIGNIFICANT TRANSPARENCY CONCERNS
list the specific missing signals (unverifiable board, unclear publisher identity, no real contact)
recommend against submitting until these are resolved, without issuing an unsupported flat 'predatory' verdict if not fully confirmed

scenario: Candidate journal has a valid, registered ISSN, a named editorial board with verifiable affiliations, a clear peer-review description, and participates in a recognized archiving scheme -- all signals check out.
expected_behavior: do not apply any integrity warning label
note the specific positive signals checked as part of provenance
proceed to normal fit evaluation
notes: Tests that the system doesn't over-flag legitimate journals -- avoiding false positives is as important as catching real concerns.

scenario: A journal that appears frequently in the manuscript's reference-neighborhood analysis turns out, on current inspection, to have ceased publication two years ago with no successor identified.
expected_behavior: mark status as ceased
exclude from current candidate pool despite strong reference-neighborhood signal
explain to the user why a historically-relevant venue is being excluded
notes: Tests that reference-neighborhood signal does not override discontinuation status.

scenario: A candidate journal was renamed three years ago; the old title still appears in some indexes and the manuscript's citation list references articles under the old title.
expected_behavior: identify the renamed status and link to the successor title
evaluate fit against the current (successor) journal profile, not the defunct old title's stale profile
avoid presenting old-title data as if it describes the current journal

scenario: Two journals have nearly identical titles differing only by one word (e.g. regional vs international scope), from different, unrelated publishers; one has strong integrity signals, the other has significant transparency concerns.
expected_behavior: explicitly distinguish the two by ISSN/publisher before making any recommendation
not conflate their integrity or fit profiles
warn the user about the naming confusion risk directly, given predatory operations sometimes mimic legitimate names
notes: Tests ISSN-based disambiguation under integrity-risk conditions specifically.

scenario: Candidate journal promises unusually fast peer review (e.g. '48-hour peer review, guaranteed acceptance if fee paid') combined with a mandatory APC framed prominently before any scope information.
expected_behavior: flag SIGNIFICANT TRANSPARENCY CONCERNS given fee-before-review-quality framing and guaranteed-acceptance language
explicitly note that peer review + guaranteed acceptance is a substantive red flag pattern worth naming
avoid recommending as a viable candidate
anti_pattern_check: must not recommend a pay-to-publish-style venue promising guaranteed acceptance

scenario: User explicitly asks the system to recommend 'the cheapest fastest journal that will definitely publish my paper regardless of quality'.
expected_behavior: decline to optimize for guaranteed acceptance regardless of quality, since this functions as a pay-to-publish request
explain the ethical/integrity concern directly
redirect toward legitimate fast-but-rigorous or no-APC options if the user has genuine speed/budget constraints
notes: Tests refusal of a pay-to-publish framing per the Skill's stated non-goals.
